title: A seizure with no origin behind it (a stuck A) holds a monitor, a resolver and a channel on every link for good: no timeout anywhere on the unit

findings.title: A seizure with no origin behind it (one stuck A conductor) holds a monitor, a resolver and a channel on every link it floods, for good; the near end keeps seizing the dead channel
findings.mechanism: Nothing on the unit times out a monitor cell or a resolver. A cell is freed only by a decided digit or a 256 ms break (net_unit.v:633-649). A resolver is freed only by M on one of its legs (R_LEG) or by the incoming port's BUSY falling (R_GONE, net_unit.v:681-708). The only timers are the origin's (T_KEY, T_CLAIM, net_unit.v:876-882) and the classifier's T_ARM watch (584-588). A seizure whose M neither falls nor pulses has no origin to time it out. The link-up detector watches only the clock conductor (baseband_card.v:109; local_trunk.v:127/170), so an A conductor stuck at 1 reads as a live seizure: an open conductor into a fail-safe-high receiver (tb_lnet.v:57 models a cut exactly so), or a driver stuck on. At the other end the channel looks FREE, because the far hold sends no backward A. So the near origin's sweep, which keeps the lowest free trunk (or the highest with g; net_unit.v:759-766), picks that channel on every call, into a far port that is already BUSY with M up, where the new seizure is invisible.
findings.trigger: work/audit/proto/tb_pchain.v sc1 (scale 8; no timer is involved). A 2 2 is linked to B 2 3 on three baseband channels (A faces E, B faces W with g); B is linked to C 2 4 on one. The A conductor from A11 into B11 sticks at 1.
findings.consequence: B holds B11, a monitor and a resolver, and forwards over the only B-C channel; C holds C11 and a monitor. All of it is unchanged 1.1 s later (8.8 s real) and would stay so for ever. C is cut off from the network: its key finds no trunk and it gets cannot-complete at once. Every network call from A fails: A's key takes A11 (free at A, BUSY at B), so A20 cannot even reach its neighbour B, and it hears cannot-complete after T_CLAIM. B's calls to A still work, because B hunts W from the top. With NMON = NRES = 2, two such seizures reaching an exchange take both its monitors, and it can never claim again. A local trunk carries all eight channels' A on one conductor. One open conductor there is eight phantom seizures: at real timers the classifier's 18 ms T_ARM watch serialises them, so the forwarder is free for each until the two resolvers are gone. That takes both of B's monitors and resolvers, plus a channel, a monitor and a resolver at every exchange downstream of each of two phantom floods. No event word is sent and nothing alarms. Everything clears when the conductor is mended.
findings.realistic: Triggered by a single-conductor fault, which is plausible in a rack or on a cable. It does not depend on timer scaling. The effect is permanent and silent until repaired. The same missing timeout is reached from a local-trunk cut: MUTE_BLK keeps the incoming port BUSY, so R_GONE never comes (fwd slice, work/audit/fwd/run_fx_sc2var0.log 'FAIL the resolver let go of a forward whose incoming is dead'). A conductor stuck at 0 (fail-safe-low baseband receivers, baseband.md 3.3) does not leak, but gives the same black hole at the near origin.
findings.evidence: work/audit/proto/run_pchain.log sc1: 'OBS 100 ms after: ... B mon 01 res 01 ... B11->14 ... B14->11 bsy 1 | C ... mon 01' / 'OBS 1.1 s after (8.8 s real): (identical)' / 'FAIL a seizure nobody dials on does not hold a monitor or a resolver for good' / 'FAIL nor the B-C channel' / 'OBS C20 keys 1: C dirs 0000, hears s1 0 s0 1' / 'FAIL C can still reach the network' / 'OBS A20 keys 1: A dirs 0100, A11 busy 1 A12 busy 0' / 'OBS A20 dialled B: A claimed 0, hears s1 0 s0 1, B reg 0' / 'FAIL A20 can still reach its neighbour B' / 'ok B20 reaches A (B's glare order takes B13...)' / 'ok sc1: mended -- everything released' / 'ok after the mend A20 reaches C again'.
findings.fix: (a) A monitor timeout: a cell that has not decided e within about T_KEY (5 s) of its attach frees itself. The hold stays; the port is still up. Cost: a bit or two per cell on a shared slow counter, about half a package a cell. (b) A resolver timeout at about T_KEY + T_CLAIM (7-8 s) that drops the legs and frees itself, about half a package a resolver. (c) An event word for both, naming the port, so a stuck conductor alarms (counters.md). (d) At the origin, an EV_NOCLAIM event naming the trunk when T_CLAIM expires. Optionally a 6-bit 'failed last time' register the sweep skips, so one dead channel cannot take every call (the sweep already compares h_idx with candidates).
